Create a independently invented, photographically plausible complex Raypunk scene whose visible ray-age technology, optimistic atomic-era design language, and readable mechanical event can later be judged in rendered pixels. Use the attached portrait only to guide the adult subject's appearance, without claiming or evaluating identity.

Create a photorealistic editorial scene at a bright Raypunk solar-weather relay station suspended above a crimson salt desert. One unmistakably adult woman is the station mechanic, wearing an ivory flight coverall with turquoise piping and a translucent protective collar. Her appearance follows the attached portrait only as a visual reference: long, center-parted, softly wavy near-black hair, warm brown almond-shaped eyes, an oval face, softly arched brows, and natural full lips. She slides a triangular crystal key into the exposed photon semaphore while her other hand steadies a brass-edged glass lens; the machine's rotating prisms visibly reconnect three saturated light lanes across the sky to an arriving bubble-window mail rocket. Surround her with polished chrome consoles, rounded pastel enamel housings, sweeping tail fins, vacuum tubes, analog star-chart dials, atomic sunburst signage, and luminous glass conduits. Keep materials tactile, tool contact unambiguous, anatomy natural, and the scene believable as a staged location photograph.

Apply the same measurable offset, delay, dependency, correspondence, or recursion across at least three separated affected surfaces. Size and place the matched instances so their shared rule can be inferred from the image without prompt text or a caption, and keep every unaffected hand, face, object boundary, material, perspective, and light response convincingly ordinary. Choose a deliberate reveal strength: either an immediate authored contradiction or a quiet second-look contradiction. render_gates.description: Lens, sensor, exposure, and image surface read as clean photographic capture rather than a damaged display or file.
The scene establishes an immediately familiar and physically coherent baseline before the contradiction is inspected.
Exactly one spatial, temporal, causal, optical, or topological invariant supplies the governing error rule.
At least three affected surfaces repeat the same measurable displacement, lag, dependency, correspondence, or recursion.

Within every affected region, native material identity, local texture, lighting, thickness, depth, boundary shape, and occlusion remain coherent under the shared rule; source pixels or facial texture are not stamped onto unrelated surfaces.
Unaffected anatomy, objects, perspective, lighting, and materials remain internally coherent and physically plausible.

The contradiction appears at the deliberately selected reveal strength, immediate or delayed, while remaining clearly authored, subordinate to one inferable world rule, and distinguishable from generic image failure.

A screen effect, split seam, collage, visible translucent shell, enclosing splash ring, portal, magical rift, flat image-plane slice, particle dissolve, or random anomaly stack does not substitute for the repeated world rule.

Without prompt text, a caption, or metadata, a viewer can state the single failed world rule and point to at least three separated instances that share its same measurable relation; merely saying that something looks wrong fails.
An isolated malformed hand or face, fused object, broken texture or text, accidental reflection or shadow mismatch, or other familiar synthesis defect does not carry the reality-error concept.
